claim_verdict.closest_single_product: Paperclip (open-source, MIT; not on the competitor matrix) - materially closer than any matrix vendor
claim_verdict.what_it_has: Staff: agents with roles, titles, reporting lines, job descriptions, monthly budgets, cost per agent/task/project, board-approved hiring. Shared skills: write-once org-wide skills assigned company-wide or per role, versioned like code, cited in run logs, with a Skill Studio (v2026.831.0). Ledger: immutable activity log of mutating actions, cost events and approvals, 'every decision explained', cache-adjusted cost ledger, revisioned config with rollback. Ladder: RFC #379 supervised/autonomous auto-promotion and demotion from run history with a working implementation claimed (2026-03-09), and 'standard-trust' scopes in v2026.817.0; agent-to-agent review verdict policies with capped rounds. Among matrix vendors the closest are Copilot Studio + Agent 365 (NL creation, connected agents, registry, identity, Evaluate) and Salesforce Agentforce (session tracing of subagents, credits per agent, Testing Center judge).
claim_verdict.what_it_lacks: Its staff routes by org-chart reporting lines, so every agent's data names its manager, and there is no capability broker; its skills are SKILL.md procedures rather than atomic identity/knowledge/behavior/intent/guardrails/format rows assembled into each prompt through capabilities, so an edit cannot be re-judged per carrier; its ledger has no decision rows with a 72-hour reversal window and before-images; its trust level is computed from run success counts, not from an independent verifier's verdicts on outputs, is not published with verdict history, and reversals are not inputs. No matrix vendor has a trust ladder at all; none has a cross-agent decision ledger with a reversal window; none shows a skill edit's before-and-after across agents; none exposes a record of its own governance agents building the product.
